title: Process-Technology Co-optimization for 2D-FETs
authors: Shao-Heng Yang, Jainil Dharmil Shah, Mayukh Das, Yuanqiu Tan, Hao-Yu Lan, Hsing-Chien Chien, Himani Jawa, Shalini Tripathi, Marco Antonio Villena, Xiangyu Wu, Daire Cott, Kaustav Banerjee, Pierre Morin, César Javier Lockhart de la Rosa, Gaurav Thareja, Dennis Lin, Joerg Appenzeller, Zhihong Chen
abstract: We present the first experimental machine learning (ML)-enabled Process-Technology Co-Optimization (PTCO) framework for optimizing 2D transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) FET fabrication directly from statistically meaningful experimental data rather than pure simulation data. We first introduce a transition voltage metric, VTrans, to quantify the gate voltage required for off-to-on switching and reveal its direct correlation with subthreshold swing (SS), highlighting an overlooked switching characteristic that governs both off-state and on-state performance. By integrating automated metric extraction, multi-objective recipe ranking, and predictive modeling, our framework uncovers hidden process-performance correlations and predicts the performance of unexplored fabrication recipes from limited experimental data. Experimental validation shows close agreement with ML predictions, thus demonstrating the framework's ability to efficiently guide gate stack optimization through iterative experimental feedback.
summary: This paper presents a novel, machine learning-enabled framework for Process-Technology Co-optimization (PTCO) applied to 2D TMD FETs. It introduces a new diagnostic metric, Transition Voltage ($	ext{V}_{	ext{Trans}}$), and uses GPR alongside multi-objective ranking to predict device performance from limited experimental data. The framework proves its utility by accurately guiding the optimization of gate stack recipes.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of optimizing the fabrication process and technology parameters (PTCO) for 2D TMD FETs, as performance is highly sensitive to process variations and existing ML methods often rely on incomplete simulation data.
main_result: The developed ML-enabled PTCO framework successfully guides gate-stack optimization by predicting performance for untested recipes, confirming that device performance is governed by complex interactions among process parameters.
method: The authors developed an experimental data-driven framework combining automated metric extraction, a Fuzzy TOPSIS multi-objective ranking scheme, and Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) for predictive modeling.
model_or_system: The physical system is 2D transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) Field-Effect Transistors (FETs). The optimization targets the gate stack recipe, which is defined by 7 key fabrication parameters.
key_observables: Key observables include the on-current ($	ext{I}_{	ext{ON}}$), Subthreshold Swing (SS), and a novel Transition Voltage ($	ext{V}_{	ext{Trans}}$).
important_parameters: The optimization is governed by the interaction of 7 key fabrication parameters defining the gate stack recipes.
main_assumptions: The framework assumes that performance can be accurately modeled and predicted from statistically meaningful experimental data, allowing for iterative refinement.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the need for $	ext{V}_{	ext{Trans}}$ in 2D devices, the extraction process for $	ext{V}_{	ext{Trans}}$, and comparisons showing how the ML-predicted ranking aligns with experimental validation, emphasizing coupled parameter effects.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the PTCO framework, details the extraction of $	ext{V}_{	ext{Trans}}$ alongside SS and $	ext{I}_{	ext{ON}}$, utilizes Fuzzy TOPSIS for multi-objective ranking, and validates the predictive power of the ML model using experimental feedback.
why_interesting: While focused on semiconductor device physics, the core methodology—using ML to map complex, high-dimensional process parameter spaces to performance metrics—is highly relevant to modeling complex quantum or many-body systems where experimental characterization is difficult.

Fig. 4 shows the corresponding transfer characteristics measured at VDS = 0.1V. Although devices with comparable SS generally exhibit comparable VTrans., distinct recipe-dependent clusters emerge, indicating that fabrication processes simultaneously influence off-state and the transition toward the on-state. This observation suggests that VTrans provides complementary information beyond conventional transistor metrics and serves as an additional optimization objective for process optimization.
